record.context_brief: Extremal cp-rank of the average mixing matrix
record.original_question: For a graph whose average mixing matrix Mc is completely positive, determine exactly when the completely positive rank of Mc is equal to n, the number of vertices. Here the completely positive rank of a completely positive matrix M is the smallest dimension d for which M is a Gram matrix of non-negative vectors in R^d.

evidence.quote: The completely positive rank (cp-rank) of a completely positive matrix M is the smallest dimension d for which M is a Gram matrix of non-negative vectors in R^d.
4.5 Open Problem. When is the cp-rank of Mc is equal to n?

artifact.self_contained_problem:
Let G be a simple graph on n vertices with adjacency matrix A, and let A = Σ_r λ_r E_r be its spectral decomposition, where the E_r are the orthogonal projectors onto the eigenspaces of A. The average mixing matrix of the continuous-time quantum walk on G is defined as
   M_c = Σ_r E_r ∘ E_r,
where ∘ denotes the Schur (entrywise) product. A symmetric n×n matrix M is called completely positive if there exists an n×d entrywise-nonnegative matrix B such that M = BB^T; the completely positive rank (cp-rank) of M is the smallest such d, equivalently the smallest d such that M is the Gram matrix of n nonnegative vectors in R^d.

Assume G is a graph for which M_c is completely positive. Characterize exactly those graphs G for which the cp-rank of M_c equals n.
artifact.status_search_result: The question of characterizing graphs whose average mixing matrix has cp-rank equal to n is stated as an open problem in the literature on average mixing matrices of continuous-time quantum walks. No published characterization was located; related work treats cp-rank bounds for general completely positive matrices but not specifically this extremal case for M_c.

status_evidence.title: A New Perspective on the Average Mixing Matrix
status_evidence.snippet: The average mixing matrix arises from continuous-time quantum walks; connections to graph structure and spectral data are studied.
status_evidence.claim: Background on the average mixing matrix M_c associated with a graph.

status_evidence.title: CP-Rank chapter, Copositive and Completely Positive Matrices
status_evidence.snippet: Surveys the cp-rank of completely positive matrices, general bounds and graph-theoretic results.
status_evidence.claim: General theory of cp-rank does not provide a specific characterization for cp-rank(M_c) = n.
